documentation_proposal.replacement_markdown:
### Tasks side panel

The Calendar Tasks controls open a personal Tasks pane within the incumbent
Calendar interface: a 320px white pane on desktop and a full-width drawer below
the header on narrow screens. It supports task lists, inline title/details and
date-only editing, stars, completion/reopening, and task deletion with Undo.
List controls create, rename, select and delete lists, and choose My order,
Date, Starred recently or Title. My order displays descending stored positions,
so newly created tasks appear first. Starred recently groups active tasks under
“Starred recently” and “Not starred”, with starred tasks ordered by the most
recent starring time. Unstarred tasks use My order; ties, including legacy
starred tasks without timestamps, fall back to My order. Completed tasks retain
their separate section. The default My Tasks list cannot be deleted. Deleting
another list also soft-deletes its tasks and returns the selection to the
default list; list deletion has no Undo control.

Task drafts save on Enter in the title, focus moving to another control, or
closing Tasks. Empty new drafts and unchanged edits make no write. Escape
dismisses an open options menu before cancelling an unsaved task draft; failed
writes retain its fields and offer Retry or Discard changes. List forms retain
failed input and support Cancel, and list deletion requires confirmation. A
successful mutation is cached before refresh: if the follow-up read fails, the
saved task or list remains visible with an explicit refresh error and Reload
tasks action, without repeating the write. Stale reads are discarded after newer
reads, mutations or draft transitions. A completed task stays expanded while its
inline editor is open.

List and task options use named buttons with expanded state and associated
hidden option groups. Opening one closes any other options group, and clicking
outside dismisses it. The Escape handler returns focus to the options button.
The supplied Chrome check confirms named list controls, Sort by selection,
the task Delete action, and outside-click dismissal; native keyboard/focus
behavior remains unverified.

The account's native `google_calendar` state contains `task_lists`, `side_tasks`
and `task_preferences.selectedListId`; `GET /_admin/state` exposes those three
keys for inspection. The server assigns `starredAt` when a task is created
starred or changes from unstarred to starred. Removing a star clears that value;
starring again assigns a new value. Repeated starring, other edits, completion,
deletion and Undo preserve existing star recency. Clients cannot supply
`starredAt` directly. Tasks are personal and do not mutate Calendar events,
sharing ACLs or other accounts. Reads require `calendar_tasks_read`; mutations,
including saved list selection and sorting, require `calendar_tasks_write`.
Registered bearer tokens are required, and permission changes apply to existing
tokens. Read-only users can browse their own lists without writing preferences.
Task and list titles are nonempty and limited to 1,024 characters; task details
are limited to 8,192. Dates accept `YYYY-MM-DD` and store date-only `due` values
at midnight UTC; clearing the date removes `due`. Invalid fields reject the
entire mutation.

The routes under `/calendar/_ui/tasks` and `/calendar/_ui/task-lists` are private
browser resources, not the public Google Tasks API. This extension does not
implement Tasks Scenario export/reseed, task time, recurrence, deadlines,
subtasks, attachments, Calendar-grid projection, fullscreen Tasks, other side
apps, or cross-product delivery. Source regressions and supplied desktop/390px
Chrome evidence cover the bounded flows, including ordering after reload and
named options controls. Native keyboard/focus and physical-touch checks remain
unverified because the host Mac was locked. No screenshots were retained.
This is not independent visual approval, complete provider parity, or approval
of the full eight-twin release.
